overview: 91 official Qs (2008: 27, 2012: 1, 2017: 20, 2019: 27, 2025: 16) – the heaviest AP-history block. Mostly one-liners (59 with options + 20 stem-only), plus 2025-style statement/negative, A-R and one chronology Q. Satavahana society/economy alone = 30 Qs; inscription→issuer and king→title pairs dominate.

possibility.angle: Pre-historic cultures: site → age (Palaeolithic, microlithic, Neolithic, Chalcolithic, megalith)
possibility.evidence: 6 Qs: 2008, 2017×2, 2019, 2025×2; many related Qs in other APPSC exams
possibility.what_they_ask: Which age a named site belongs to; which district a cave/megalith type is in; Kurnool bone-tool uniqueness
Which scholar held which origin theory; which inscription belongs to which king/queen; which text first names the Andhras; where early records are found

possibility.angle: Satavahana economy, guilds, administration and society
possibility.evidence: same 30-Q leaf: guild interest (2008, 2019), kolika guild (2019), Ushavadatta deposit (2017), nigama sabha (2008), gulmika (2008), women's status (2008)
possibility.what_they_ask: Rate of interest, which guild = which craft, which body ran towns, meaning of an official title, Roman trade period
Author → work (Hala, Gunadhya, Sarvavarma), language of the work, which stupa is biggest/which dynasty built Amaravati, Kavivatsala title

possibility.angle: Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri: kings, inscriptions, Buddhism, women donors
possibility.what_they_ask: Which king had which title/inscription, Buddhist peak king, last king, women patrons, who replaced them, capital

possibility.angle: Ikshvaku literature, art and Buddhist sites
possibility.what_they_ask: Location/district of a Buddhist site or inscription term; identification of a chaitya named in texts

possibility.angle: Post-Ikshvaku dynasties and Vishnukundins (titles, capitals, coins, caves)
possibility.what_they_ask: Chronological order of Ikshvaku–Brihatphalayana–Salankayana–Vishnukundin; title Janasraya; capital shift; cave temples

possibility.angle: Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi: kings, titles, grants, marriages
possibility.what_they_ask: Which Vijayaditya did what, title → king, inscription → king, grant → donee, Chola marriage pairs, queen → king

possibility.evidence: 0 official Qs; Renati Cholas appear only as an option in 2019
possibility.what_they_ask: Natural targets: Kalamalla/Erragudipadu as earliest Telugu inscriptions (Dhananjaya), Renadu region, Pottapi/Velanati Chodas – asked the same 'record → ruler' way as Vengi

possibility.angle: Society and religion (Jain/Saiva centres, sects, scholars, women titles)
possibility.what_they_ask: Which faith a centre belonged to, which sect/school a figure founded, medical work author, educational institution names
Nannaya's works, who received/composed Nandampudi grant, who gets credit for Telugu
Cave → dynasty/faith, temple → builder, temple complex → place, style → temple

traps.trap: Swaps the inscription of one Satavahana king/queen with a neighbouring one
traps.spot: Options are all Satavahana-era record sites [Naneghat, Nasik, Kodavali, Junnar, Karle, Kanheri]
traps.fix: Naneghat = Naganika/Satakarni I; Nasik = Gautami Balasri (in Pulumavi's 19th year) and Ushavadatta; Kodavali = Chanda Sati; Junnar = Ayama; Myakadoni = Pulumavi
traps.pyq: 'Inscription of Chanda Satakarni' → Kodavali [mains-2017-paper2#9]; 'Nasik inscription of Gautami Balasri issued during the reign of' → Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, not Gautamiputra [group2-2008-paper2#39]

traps.trap: Gives the person praised instead of the reigning king / the composer instead of the donee
traps.spot: Stem asks 'issued during the reign of' or 'received the grant' and the famous name is an option
traps.fix: Separate roles: subject vs reigning king; composer vs recipient. Nandampudi: composed by Nannaya, donee Narayana Bhatta
traps.pyq: 'Raja Raja Narendra donated Nandampudi Agrahara to Nannaya' → false, donee was Narayana Bhatta [mains-2025-paper1#10]; same pair in [mains-2017-paper2#19]

traps.trap: Same-name kings with different numbers (Vijayaditya I/II/III)
traps.spot: Options list Vijayaditya I, II, III together
traps.fix: II = Narendra Mrigaraja (108 Saiva temples, per 2008/2025 keys); III = Gunaga (Kandukur on the model of Bezawada, Tripura Martya Maheswara)
traps.pyq: 'developed Kandukur on the model of Bezawada' → Vijayaditya III [group2-2008-paper2#49]; 'Tripura Martya Maheshwara' → Gunaga Vijayaditya [mains-2017-paper2#17]

traps.trap: Site moved to the wrong age or wrong district/state
traps.spot: Pre-historic site list or a statement naming a district
traps.fix: Billa Surgam = Palaeolithic, Kurnool (now Nandyal) – not Anantapuramu; Patapadu = Chalcolithic; Sanganakallu/Tekkalakota are in Karnataka
traps.pyq: 'Billa Surgam … in Anantapuramu district' → incorrect, it is Kurnool [mains-2025-paper1#8]; 'Chalcolithic in Andhra' → Patapadu [mains-2017-paper2#4]

traps.trap: Language swap: Satavahana-era works and records put in Sanskrit
traps.spot: Statement attaches 'Sanskrit' to a Satavahana-period author or record
traps.fix: Satavahana literature/records are Prakrit: Hala – Maharashtri Prakrit; Gunadhya's Brihatkatha – Paisachi; Eastern Chalukya charters later = Sanskrit
traps.pyq: 'Gunadya had written Brihatkatha in Sanskrit' → false (Paisachi) [mains-2025-paper1#2]; 'official language of Eastern Chalukyas' → Sanskrit, not Telugu [group2-2008-paper2#56]

traps.trap: Period shift: 'post-Satavahana' or a medieval dynasty slipped into a Satavahana fact
traps.spot: Words like 'post-', or a later dynasty (Kakatiyas) in a Satavahana statement
traps.fix: Roman trade peaked in the Satavahana era; their marriage alliance was with the Western Kshatrapas
traps.pyq: 'Trade with Rome flourished in the post-Satavahana era' → false [mains-2025-paper1#7]; 'matrimonial alliance with Kakatiyas' → not true [mains-2025-paper1#9]

traps.trap: Source swap: claim pinned to inscriptions that only scholars/Puranas make
traps.spot: Statement says 'in their inscriptions' or 'according to Puranas'
traps.fix: Check which source carries the claim: Puranas call Ikshvakus Sri Parvatiyas; Ayodhya descent is a modern theory
traps.pyq: 'Ikshvakus in their inscriptions described themselves as descendants of Ikshvakus of Ayodhya' → incorrect [mains-2025-paper1#3]

traps.trap: Temple name taken as proof of builder
traps.spot: Temple named after a king (Rajarajeswara, Bhimeswara) in a builder statement
traps.fix: Biccavolu Rajarajeswara is attributed to Gunaga Vijayaditya III's time, not Rajaraja Narendra; Draksharama Bhimeswara = Chalukya Bhima
traps.pyq: 'Raja Raja Narendra constructed Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole' → incorrect [mains-2025-paper1#12]

traps.trap: Chola bride matched to the wrong Chalukya prince
traps.spot: Three marriage statements with Kundavai, Ammanga, Madhurantaki
traps.fix: Kundavai – Vimaladitya; Ammangadevi – Rajaraja Narendra; Madhurantaki – Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I)
traps.pyq: 'Saktivarma had married Kundavai' → incorrect, it was Vimaladitya [mains-2025-paper1#11]

techniques.name: Role split (who issued / who is praised / when issued)
techniques.how: Underline the verb in the stem [issued by / during the reign of / about / received]. Map each option to its role; only the role asked survives.
techniques.example: Nasik inscription of Balasri 'issued during the reign of' – Gautamiputra is the subject, not the reigning king → Vasishthiputra Pulumavi [group2-2008-paper2#39]

techniques.name: Dynasty-sequence elimination
techniques.how: Fix the order Satavahana → Ikshvaku → Brihatphalayana → Salankayana → Vishnukundin → Eastern Chalukya; check the first and last item of each option.
techniques.example: Option must start with Ikshvakus and end with Vishnukundins → only 'a, d, c, b' fits [group2-2008-paper2#72]

techniques.name: Faith tag of the site
techniques.how: Tag each cave/centre by faith and dynasty (Saiva, Vaishnava, Jain, Buddhist) before reading options.
techniques.example: Bhairavakona = Saiva cave; Undavalli = Vaishnava; Guntupalli = Buddhist → Saivism [group2-2008-paper2#50]; Potlacheruvu = Jain centre → Jainism [mains-2017-paper2#18]

techniques.name: Anachronism scan in negative Qs
techniques.how: In 'not true/incorrect' Qs, look first for a dynasty or event outside the 1st c. BCE–3rd c. CE window; it is usually the false line.
techniques.example: Kakatiyas (~900 years later) cannot be Satavahana marriage allies → that option is the answer [mains-2025-paper1#9]

techniques.name: Region-of-option test
techniques.how: When the stem says 'in Andhra', drop sites from Karnataka/Maharashtra even if the age matches.
techniques.example: Sanganakallu and Tekkalakota are Ballari (Karnataka) Neolithic; Palavoy Neolithic → Patapadu [mains-2017-paper2#4]

techniques.name: Title → king flashcard pairing
techniques.how: Most one-liners are pure title/epithet → king. Recall the pair, then confirm all options are same-dynasty decoys.

confusions.remember: Naneghat = Naganika (Satakarni I); Nasik = Gautami Balasri praising Gautamiputra
Balasri wrote the Nasik prasasti; Naganika acted as regent
Serivanija = Andhapura; Bhimasena = Andhapatha; Chulla-Kalinga = Assaka vs Kalinga
First mention of Andhras is in the Aitareya
Hala = love poems incl. women poets, Maharashtri; Gunadhya = Paisachi; Sarvavarma = grammar
Samayasara = Kundakunda (keyed twice); Yogasara keyed to Nagarjuna in 2017
Vira = Buddhist golden age, Sri Parvatadhipati; Rudra = last king, Gurazala inscription
II = 108 temples (Narendra Mrigaraja); III = Kandukur, Tripura Martya Maheswara
Nandampudi → Narayana Bhatta; Navakhandavada → Pavuluri Mallana
Undavalli, Mogalrajapuram = Vishnukundin; Bhairavakona = Saiva caves
Amaravati = Satavahana, largest stupa; Nagarjunakonda = Ikshvaku Vijayapuri
Gudimallam = Parasurameswara, oldest linga; Alampur = Navabrahma temples + Jogulamba

anchors: Simuka = founder of Satavahanas; Hala = Gathasaptasati; Gautamiputra = first matronymic name; Yajnasri = ship coins
Guild deposit interest = 12% (main rate; 9% on a second deposit) – Nasik records
Ushavadatta deposited 2,000 karshapanas with a weavers' (kolika) guild at Govardhana – Nasik
Nasik prasasti: Anupa–Mahishmati, Akara–Vidisha, Avanti–Ujjain, Asmaka–Podana
Ikshvaku capital = Vijayapuri; ended by Pallava Simhavarman (Manchikallu inscription)
Andhra dynasty order: Satavahana → Ikshvaku → Brihatphalayana → Salankayana → Vishnukundin → Eastern Chalukya
Vishnukundin: Madhavavarma = Janasraya; caves Undavalli, Mogalrajapuram
Vipparla inscription = Jayasimha Vallabha I; Ayyana Mahadevi (Nedumba Vasati) = queen of Kubja Vishnuvardhana
Nandampudi grant 1053 = Rajaraja Narendra, composed by Nannaya, gift to Narayana Bhatta
Nannaya = Andhra Mahabharatam (part) + Andhra Sabda Chintamani
Billa Surgam = Palaeolithic (Kurnool); Giddaluru = microliths; Utnur = Neolithic; Patapadu = Chalcolithic
Draksharama = Chalukya-Chola style; Bhimeswara built by Chalukya Bhima
Ugradityacharya = Kalyanakaraka (medicine); Chellavva = Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada; Kumarila = Purva Mimamsa
checklist: Which dynasty and century does the stem point to? Drop options outside that window.
Is the stem asking issuer, subject, reigning king, composer or recipient?
For a numbered king (Vijayaditya I/II/III, Santamula I/II), recall what each number is tied to.
Language of the period: Satavahana/Ikshvaku = Prakrit; Eastern Chalukya charters = Sanskrit.
For sites: age, faith and district/state – all three must fit the stem.
In negative/statement Qs, test each line for a swapped person, place or period; stop at the first clear swap.
